notes:
Describes work, positions, or leave periods for which no salary or pay is given. Common in discussions of employment, internships, volunteer work, and leave policies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無給|むきゅう}{休暇|きゅうか}: unpaid leave
- {無給|むきゅう}のインターン: unpaid intern
- {無給|むきゅう}で{働|はたら}く: to work without pay
- {無給|むきゅう}{期間|きかん}: unpaid period
- {無給|むきゅう}{労働|ろうどう}: unpaid labor

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {有給|ゆうきゅう}: paid — the antonym; most commonly seen in {有給|ゆうきゅう}{休暇|きゅうか} (paid leave)
- {無償|むしょう}: free of charge, gratuitous — broader; can apply to goods and services, not just labor
- {無報酬|むほうしゅう}: without remuneration — more formal; emphasizes the absence of any reward

NOTE ON HOMOPHONE:
Not to be confused with {無休|むきゅう} (no days off, always open), which has the same reading but different meaning and kanji.

definitions.explanation: receiving no pay or salary for work or a position; without monetary compensation

examples.japanese: {無給|むきゅう}のインターンとして{働|はたら}く。
examples.english: To work as an unpaid intern.

examples.japanese: {育児|いくじ}{休暇|きゅうか}は{無給|むきゅう}になる{場合|ばあい}がある。
examples.english: Parental leave may be unpaid in some cases.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{無給|むきゅう}で{地域|ちいき}のボランティア{活動|かつどう}に{参加|さんか}している。
examples.english: He participates in local volunteer activities without pay.

examples.japanese: {無給|むきゅう}{休暇|きゅうか}を{取得|しゅとく}して{海外|かいがい}に{留学|りゅうがく}することにした。
examples.english: I decided to take unpaid leave and study abroad.
